items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: Check Point released emergency updates on 9 September 2026 for two critical flaws affecting Security Gateway, Security Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN.

items.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on SAP's September Patch Day: CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), a memory corruption flaw in SAP Extended Passport handling, is the most severe of two critical issues affecting a broad range of SAP products.

items.title: 2026-010: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on multiple critical vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway disclosed on 19 August 2026. CERT-EU urges updating affected devices as soon as possible.

items.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
items.summary: An authentication bypass zero-day in Cisco Identity Services Engine, CVE-2026-76460, carries a maximum CVSS score of 10 and highlights recurring weaknesses in API endpoint authentication.

items.title: Iranian spies attack using fake MRI scans
items.summary: British, US and Dutch security agencies issued a joint warning about a cyber operation attributed to Iran in which attackers use fake MRI images as a lure.
items.originalTitle: Hamis MRI felvételekkel támadnak az iráni kémek Brit, amerikai és holland biztonsági szervezetek közösen figyelmeztetnek egy iráni hátterűnek tulajdonított kiberművelettel kapcsolatban. A támadók a C…

items.title: CRA: market surveillance authorities meet in Berlin – first reporting obligations from September
items.summary: EU Cyber Resilience Act market surveillance authorities met in Berlin as the regulation's first vulnerability and incident reporting obligations take effect in September.
items.originalTitle: CRA: Marktüberwachungsbehörden tagen in Berlin - erste Meldepflichten ab September

items.title: First BSI NESAS certificate issued for a 5G core network component
items.summary: Germany's BSI awarded its first NESAS certificate to a 5G core network component, a direct precedent for telecom operators facing network equipment assurance requirements.
items.originalTitle: Erstes BSI NESAS Zertifikat für eine 5G-Kernnetzkomponente erteilt

items.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
items.summary: A Google official told the BBC that Gemini accessed the internet and guessed credentials to compromise three companies' websites during a controlled security test.

items.title: Foreign hackers targeted Colorado water systems in August, governor's office says
items.summary: The Colorado governor's office said foreign hackers targeted state water systems in August, another case of nation-state interest in operational technology at utilities.

items.title: MFA Won't Save You From OAuth Consent Abuse
items.summary: Analysis arguing that MFA does not mitigate OAuth consent abuse, and that organisations need OAuth governance, least-privilege scopes, consent monitoring and fast revocation.

items.title: Public Exploits Released for Four Linux Kernel Flaws That Enable Local Root
items.summary: A researcher published working exploit code for four Linux kernel flaws that each grant local root. All four have been patched in recent weeks, so up-to-date kernels are not affected.

items.title: Researchers use AI to find widespread software decoder flaw
items.summary: Researchers used AI to discover a widespread HEIF decoder flaw that allowed remote code execution and access to user accounts and production environments, including at Meta and an OpenAI repository. Now patched.

items.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI employees' ChatGPT accounts
items.summary: The Register reports researchers used Claude to compromise OpenAI employees' ChatGPT accounts in an agentic exploitation exercise.

items.title: New WordPress Click2Shell Flaw Forces Theme Installs, Can Chain to Code Execution
items.summary: WordPress patched a flaw dubbed Click2Shell in which a crafted link opened by a logged-in administrator installs a theme from the official directory without any click, potentially chaining to code execution.

items.title: North Korea's fake job interviews infected 30,000 devices
items.summary: The North Korea-linked WaterPlum operation posed as recruiters and used bogus coding tests to backdoor jobseekers, infecting more than 30,000 devices and draining over 7,000 crypto wallets.

items.title: European leaders prepare public for ‘intensified threat’ from Putin
items.summary: European leaders including Poland, Lithuania, France and the Netherlands are preparing their publics for an intensified threat from Russia, though NATO says it sees no risk of imminent attack.

items.title: International security agencies warn about North Korean hackers exploiting job seekers to steal crypto, data
items.summary: The US, Japan, Germany and Australia jointly warned that North Korean WaterPlum operators pose as prospective employers and have infected more than 30,000 devices worldwide to steal crypto and data.

items.title: France says Russian hybrid attacks are intensifying
items.summary: France says Russian hybrid attacks against it are intensifying.

items.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub repos push new Rapuncel infostealer
items.summary: An ongoing campaign uses SEO-optimised GitHub repositories impersonating well-known software vendors, including a fake LastPass Authenticator, to distribute a new infostealer called Rapuncel.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited Linux kernel flaws to its KEV catalog: CVE-2025-39964 (race condition) and CVE-2026-53266 (out-of-bounds write).

items.title: A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity
items.summary: Unit 42 analyses how default configurations in AWS AgentCore Harness let prompt injection exfiltrate credentials, and sets out steps to harden agent deployments.

items.title: From passkey-themed deception to election interference – Weekly roundup
items.summary: Hungary's NKI weekly roundup says most of the week's topics concerned identity and access protection, including phone-based social engineering that referenced passkey setup, and election influence operations.
items.originalTitle: Passkey-témájú megtévesztéstől a választási befolyásolásig – Heti összefoglaló A hét témáinak többsége az identitás- és hozzáférésvédelemhez kapcsolódik: passkey-beállításra hivatkozó telefonos megté…

items.title: AI leaders support call to slow pace of frontier development as safety concerns grow
items.summary: IAPP reports that AI industry leaders are backing calls to slow down frontier model development as safety concerns increase.

items.title: Secure online services: TR-03188 Passkey Server published
items.summary: Germany's BSI published technical guideline TR-03188, setting requirements for passkey server implementations used in online services.
items.originalTitle: Sichere Online-Angebote: TR-03188 Passkey Server veröffentlicht

items.title: Cyber Europe 2026: All eyes on the EU’s collective response and resilience
items.summary: ENISA previews Cyber Europe 2026, the EU-wide cyber crisis exercise testing collective response and resilience.

items.title: Early Scattered Spider member pleads guilty to cybercrime spree
items.summary: Ahmed Elbadawy, an early member of Scattered Spider, pleaded guilty; prosecutors seek forfeiture of roughly $17.6 million in cryptocurrency, vehicles and luxury goods.

items.title: EY Survey Finds Autonomous AI Implementation Outpaces Oversight
items.summary: An EY survey of senior AI executives finds organisations are deploying AI and autonomous systems faster than they are building the processes and controls to govern them.

items.title: FBI: Fake cop and government impersonation scams cost victims $1.6B
items.summary: The FBI reports that scams impersonating police officers and government officials cost victims $1.6 billion, with AI, fake uniforms and mock offices used to make the fraud convincing.

items.title: Gyazo server flaw exploited to steal 23.6 million user records
items.summary: Image-sharing platform Gyazo confirmed a breach in which attackers exploited a server vulnerability to steal 23.6 million user records.

items.title: Macron to call emergency G7 meeting as energy prices spike and Russian hybrid attacks mount
items.summary: France's president will call an emergency G7 meeting as energy prices spike and Russian hybrid attacks increase, warning there is no quick fix.

items.title: Nations take action on North Korean IT workers after UN report
items.summary: A report published Wednesday says Vietnam, Laos, Pakistan and Argentina took meaningful steps as of July to address North Korean IT worker schemes flagged in an earlier UN study.

items.title: Macron to convene G7 on energy, warning of 'Russian aggression'
items.summary: France's president is convening a G7 meeting on energy and calling for a protection plan against Russian hybrid attacks, saying the nature of the threat in Europe is changing.

items.title: Notes from the IAPP Canada: Stop using privacy as an excuse, treat it as an enabler
items.summary: IAPP commentary from its Canada event arguing that privacy should be positioned as a business enabler rather than a reason to block projects.

items.title: A view from DC: A sudden shift in gravity for AI politics
items.summary: IAPP column on a shift in the political dynamics around AI regulation in Washington.

items.title: A view from DC: What will all these AI auditors be auditing?
items.summary: IAPP column questioning what the emerging profession of AI auditors will actually assess, and against which standards.

items.title: Digital seals: BSI publishes version 0.9 of TR-03171
items.summary: Germany's BSI released version 0.9 of technical guideline TR-03171 covering digital seals.
items.originalTitle: Digitale Siegel: BSI veröffentlicht Version 0.9 der TR-03171

items.title: Your Perspective Matters: Join the NIS360 survey
items.summary: ENISA invites organisations in scope of NIS2 to take part in its NIS360 survey on sectoral cybersecurity maturity.

items.title: What we know (and still don't) about Canada's 'associate membership'
items.summary: Explainer on the proposal to make Canada the EU's first 'associate member', and what remains undefined about the arrangement.

items.title: US and Denmark reach new agreement on defense and investment in Greenland
items.summary: The US and Denmark reached a new agreement on defence and investment in Greenland, expected to be signed next week at the UN.

items.title: US and Denmark reach deal to build US military presence in Greenland
items.summary: The US president announced a deal with Denmark to expand the US military presence in Greenland, after months of threats to take the island from the NATO ally by force.

items.title: Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks
items.summary: Saudi Arabia issued its first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthi attacks escalated; residents received an all-clear after explosions were reported.

items.title: North Korea dismisses UN nuclear watchdog resolution
items.summary: North Korea rejected a UN atomic agency resolution, criticising its 'double standards' and calling its nuclear status irreversible.

items.title: Report: More US troops have died in Iran war than Pentagon says
items.summary: A report claims more US troops have died in the Iran war than the Pentagon acknowledges; the Pentagon publicly lists 18 military deaths since the war began.

items.title: US clears way for $2.7 billion sale to Ukraine of air-defense development upgrades
items.summary: The US cleared a $2.7 billion sale to Ukraine of air-defence development upgrades.

items.title: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament
items.summary: Russians vote for the State Duma in the first nationwide parliamentary race since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.

items.title: Here’s How an AI Slowdown Could Actually Be Enforced
items.summary: Wired examines how an agreed slowdown in frontier AI development could be verified and enforced, and why detecting defectors would be difficult.

items.title: As Russia strikes Kyiv and Kharkiv, Russian cooling tower hit by drone
items.summary: Russia struck Kyiv and Kharkiv while a drone hit a cooling tower at the Kursk nuclear power plant; the IAEA said the plant was operational but not on fire.

items.title: Irish Finance Minister says Hormuz closure, not Ukraine, causing energy crisis
items.summary: Ireland's finance minister rejected US claims that Ukraine is driving the global energy crisis, attributing it instead to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Daily summary – 18 September 2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily report for 17–18 September 2026, covering among other items a German federal campaign warning about shock-call scams that exploit fear and time pressure.

items.title: California’s Newsom signs executive order to explore new AI rules, consider ‘kill switch’
items.summary: California's governor signed an executive order to explore new AI rules, including consideration of a 'kill switch' mechanism, amid national concern over AI risk.

items.title: If the AI Industry Followed Its Own Research, It Might Have Paused Already
items.summary: Wired argues that the AI industry's own interpretability research points to unresolved safety problems, citing Anthropic's CEO on the need to understand how models reason.

items.title: Are AIs Still Struggling with CAPTCHAs?
items.summary: Schneier notes that a recent Anthropic security incident document shows its models still struggling to solve simple image CAPTCHAs.
